title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: predestination is ordination with infallible event; reprobation denies unfrustrable special operation — Bellarmine: God not bound to give sufficient grace to all
pass_a_gloss: The reason on both sides is the same; Because predestination does not mean any ordination whatsoever unto a supernatural end through media however sufficient, but an ordination coupled with an infallible issue and event; nor does reprobation deny every ordination unto a supernatural end, but an unfrustrable ordination from the device and special operation of the ordaining God, producing the very event of salvation. Finally, that sufficient media unto salvation are given unto all is not proved with as much facility as it is affirmed with confidence. I will not now enter this dispute, because for the solution of the argument proposed (as you have received) it is not necessary. This only I will note, that Bellarmine, who defends this opinion concerning sufficient grace, first grants us that there would be no iniquity in God if he denied this sufficient grace unto some or unto all, De grat. et lib. arb. l. 2. cap. 4. Hence we gather that God is bound unto this by no pact or promise: How then do the adversaries dare to promise unto all and singular sufficient grace, which God has not promised?
pass_b_english: The reason is the same either way. Predestination is not just any ordination to a supernatural end by media however sufficient — it is ordination joined to an infallible outcome. Reprobation does not deny every ordination to a supernatural end, but the unfrustrable ordination that comes from the ordaining God's device and special operation producing the very event of salvation. Finally: that sufficient media of salvation are given to all is asserted with more confidence than it is proved with ease. I will not enter that dispute now — it is not needed to solve the argument before us. One note only: Bellarmine, who defends this sufficient-grace view, first grants that God would do no injustice if he denied that sufficient grace to some or to all (De grat. et lib. arb. 2.4). So God is bound to it by no pact or promise. How then dare the adversaries promise every person sufficient grace that God never promised?
source_text: Ratio utrobique eadem est; Quia praedestinatio non dicit quamlibet ordinationem ad finem supernaturalem per media quantovis sufficientia, sed ordinationem cum exitu et eventu infallibili copulatam; neque reprobatio negat omnem ordinationem ad finem supernaturalem, sed ordinationem infrustrabilem ex inventione et speciali operatione Dei ordinantis, ipsum salutis eventum producentem. Denique, sufficientia media ad salutem omnibus dari, non tanta facilitate probatur quanta confidentia affirmatur. Non jam ingrediar hanc disputationem, quia ad solutionem argumenti propositi (uti accepistis) non est necesse. Illud solummodo annotabo, Bellarminum, qui hanc de sufficiente gratia sententiam tuetur, primo concedere nobis, quod nulla esset in Deo iniquitas si negaret aliquibus vel omnibus hanc gratiam sufficientem, De grat. et lib. arb. l. 2. cap. 4. Hinc colligimus, Deum nullo pacto aut promissione ad hoc obligatum: Quomodo igitur adversarii audent promittere omnibus et singulis gratiam sufficientem, quam Deus non promisit?
